problem: Grow faster by lowering the barrier to try the product.
title: Mailchimp adds a free plan after eight years of charging
context: Mailchimp had charged customers for eight years and was self-funded.
decision_made: Offer a free plan, tested with pricing data to see how it might affect its paid plan, and ensure enough paying customers and cash first.
action_taken: Announced in September 2009; sources disagree whether the free limit was 500 or 2,000 contacts.
observed_outcome: One account says the user base grew five-fold from 85,000 in September 2009 to 450,000 in September 2010, adding about 30,000 free users and 4,000 paying customers each month.
lessons: A free plan can work as a marketing channel when the company has revenue to absorb the cost.
limitations: Figures were drawn from a founder's blog post cited second-hand. The free limit differs by source. The founder described freemium as marketing rather than a business model.

claims.claim_text: Mailchimp introduced a free plan in September 2009 after charging for eight years.
Mailchimp's user base reportedly grew from 85,000 to 450,000 in a year.
